newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Products Outlook - W.Coast strike seen a spur.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Products Outlook - W.Coast strike seen a spur.

text.p: Spot gasoline prices on the U.S. West Coast could skyrocket this week, propelled by low stocks and threats of a strike late Monday at Unocal Corp's four California refineries, traders and analysts said.

Refinery workers remained on the job early Monday ahead of the threatened strike. But traders in other regions watched carefully, with one Gulf Coast trader predicting West Coast gasoline will "go orbital" if 900 union workers walked out.
The Unocal plants combine to make about 20 percent of California's gasoline.

"Prices will go to Mars if there's a strike," the trader said, noting West Coast (PADD 5) gasoline supplies were down by more than 5.3 million barrels from year-ago, according to American Petroleum Institute data for the week ending March 14. That is more than half the current year-on-year U.S. gasoline shortfall of 9.7 million barrels.
Offers for CARB grade unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles rose 6.50 cents last week to 85 cents on fears of a strike and prolonged maintenance shutdowns at Mobil and Exxon.
Refinery workers say they are frustated by a recent severance package offered by Unocal, who is selling the refineries to Tosco Corp March 31.
Last week, the union rejected a final Tosco labor contract, which labor leaders say contains too many job cuts and sub-standard benefits.

Meanwhile, the cash gasoline market in New York Harbor should remain weak this week, an East Coast trader said, noting differentials on winter-grade "M5" conventional unleaded eased one cent to 5.0 cents below benchmark gasoline futures last week as the market began spurning it in favor of lower Reid Vapor Pressure "M2" grade.
NYH gasoline was also seen under downward pressure from sizeable imports of gasoline blendstocks.

But beyond the next few weeks, Bear Stearns senior analyst Frederick Leuffer said he is bullish on gasoline because of low U.S. stocks and the approach of summer driving season -- which traditionally begins on Memorial Day in late May.
"Gasoline is the only oil component with inventories that are down on a year-to-year basis," a fact he says will bode well for refining margins.
"If crude goes down, gasoline won't go down as much because of the demand and low stocks."
In the Midwest, diesel fuel prices were expected to rise in the coming weeks on emerging seasonal agricultural demand during the spring planting season, traders said.

Increased diesel fuel use by farmers also was expected to draw down inventories in the regional pipeline system and provide support for spot prices in the near term, particularly in the Midwest's Group Three market.
"That's going to pull out some of the diesel in Williams," one trader said of the Williams pipeline system, a key barometer of stocks in the lower-Midwest Group market.
The Williams pipeline system opens the week with a 33-day supply of low sulphur diesel and 25-day supply of unleaded gasoline stocks on hand, traders said.

The Williams system, a key barometer of stocks in the Group market, reported a 29-day supply of low sulphur diesel and 24-day supply of gasoline on hand as trade wound down for the week, traders said.

Chicago winter-grade unleaded gasoline demand was expected to continue to weaken after pushing bids 9.25 cents a gallon under NYMEX April unleaded ahead of the early April changeover to summer-grade specifications.
